ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A student placed 20 tobacco seeds of the same species on moist paper towels in each of two petri dishes. Dish A was wrapped completely in an opaque cover to exclude all light. Dish B was not wrapped. The dishes were placed equidistant from a light source set to a cycle of 14h of light and 10h of dark. All other conditions were the same for both dishes. The dishes were examined after seven days, and the opaque cover was permanently removed from dish A. Both dishes were returned to the light and examined again at 14 days. The following data were obtained, as shown in the figure. Based on these data, what best describes the usefulness of the yellow-leaved phenotype as a variation subject to natural selection?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: The yellow-leaved phenotype can germinate in environments without light.
